raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The API-key auth middleware is only installed in single-tokenizer mode
(`tokenizer_worker_num == 1`, see `launch_server`). When
`--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, a configured `--admin-api-key` (or `--api-key`)
is never wired into the request path, so admin-tagged management routes become
reachable without credentials. The worker init already rejected `api_key`, but
it did not reject `admin_api_key`, and only failed after startup rather than at
config-validation time.

## Modifications

- `ServerArgs.check_server_args()` now rejects a configured `api_key` /
  `admin_api_key` when `tokenizer_worker_num > 1`, failing fast at startup
  with a clear message (set `tokenizer_worker_num=1` to use API-key auth).
- Added `TestMultiTokenizerApiKeyRejected` covering: admin key rejected,
  normal key rejected, and single-worker + both keys allowed.

No changes to model/kernel/forward code or any inference path.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — this is a startup config-validation change and does not affect model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — no change to any inference or scheduling path; the guard runs once during
`check_server_args()` at launch.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
Runtime confirmation from a full-server PoC (sglang 0.5.21, PyPI, CPU device), in case it helps this get merged:

- Started with `--tokenizer-worker-num 4 --admin-api-key SECRET123` → the server boots normally to /health=200 (no fail-fast), and an **unauthenticated** `POST /flush_cache` (ADMIN_OPTIONAL route) returns **200 "Cache flushed."**; unauthenticated `GET /server_info` also returns 200 with the plaintext key in `launch_command`.
- Control on the same build: single-tokenizer with the same `--admin-api-key` → unauthenticated `POST /flush_cache` returns **401 Unauthorized`, and the same request succeeds with `Bearer SECRET123` — isolating the bypass to the `tokenizer_worker_num == 1` middleware-install condition exactly as described here.

Also worth noting while this is unmerged: in the multi-tokenizer configuration the three hicache endpoints that "check" the admin key pass for any caller, because their check only tests that the config value exists (`if not get_serving().admin_api_key: 403`, http_server.py ~:1111/:1143/:1167), not the request credentials.

Harness (localhost-only, both modes + controls) available on request.

Chengzhi Yi (GitHub @Tardfyou) — yimou@hust.edu.cn

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a validation check to reject API key configurations (`api_key` or `admin_api_key`) when running in multi-tokenizer mode (`tokenizer_worker_num > 1`), as the authentication middleware is only supported in single-tokenizer mode. It also adds corresponding unit tests to verify this behavior. The reviewer suggested using truthiness checks (`not self.api_key` and `not self.admin_api_key`) instead of explicit `None` checks to robustly handle cases where empty strings are passed as arguments.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Checking `self.api_key is None` and `self.admin_api_key is None` can cause unexpected assertion failures if these arguments are passed as empty strings (e.g., `--api-key ""` or `--admin-api-key ""`), which are functionally treated as disabled/unset in `auth.py` (using `if api_key:`). \n\nUsing `not self.api_key` and `not self.admin_api_key` is more robust and aligns with how truthiness is checked in the authentication middleware.

```suggestion
            assert not self.api_key and not self.admin_api_key, (
```

files.patch:
@@ -8507,6 +8507,13 @@ def check_server_args(self):
             self.mm_processor_worker_num >= 0
         ), "Multimodal processor worker num must >= 0"
         assert self.mm_io_worker_num >= 0, "Multimodal I/O worker num must >= 0"
+        if self.tokenizer_worker_num > 1:
+            # Multi-tokenizer workers bypass the HTTP auth middleware.
+            assert not self.api_key and not self.admin_api_key, (
+                "API key authentication (--api-key / --admin-api-key) is not "
+                "supported in multi-tokenizer mode (tokenizer_worker_num > 1). "
+                "Set tokenizer_worker_num=1 to enable API key authentication."
+            )
         self.validate_buckets_rule(
             "--prompt-tokens-buckets", self.prompt_tokens_buckets
         )

@@ -1859,5 +1859,39 @@ def test_ep_a2a_backend_ok_without_dp_attention(self):
         args._check_two_batch_overlap()
 
 
+class TestMultiTokenizerApiKeyRejected(CustomTestCase):
+    """Test API-key validation for multi-tokenizer mode."""
+
+    def test_admin_api_key_rejected_with_multiple_tokenizer_workers(self):
+        args = ServerArgs(
+            model_path="dummy", tokenizer_worker_num=2, admin_api_key="admin"
+        )
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, "multi-tokenizer mode"):
+            args.check_server_args()
+
+    def test_api_key_rejected_with_multiple_tokenizer_workers(self):
+        args = ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", tokenizer_worker_num=2, api_key="user")
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, "multi-tokenizer mode"):
+            args.check_server_args()
+
+    def test_empty_keys_allowed_with_multiple_tokenizer_workers(self):
+        args = ServerArgs(
+            model_path="dummy",
+            tokenizer_worker_num=2,
+            api_key="",
+            admin_api_key="",
+        )
+        args.check_server_args()
+
+    def test_keys_allowed_with_single_tokenizer_worker(self):
+        args = ServerArgs(
+            model_path="dummy",
+            tokenizer_worker_num=1,
+            api_key="user",
+            admin_api_key="admin",
+        )
+        args.check_server_args()
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
